text:
Maya (eng-platform): Heads-up — running a combined spot eviction + control-plane network partition game day today at 14:00 PT in us-west2. Goal: validate mixed-capacity pool failover (spot -> on-demand -> cross-region) and confirm autoscaler/cooldown behavior under network blips. Expected run ~30m. Success criteria listed below.

Jordan (eng-sre): ok, what are the exact success criteria?

Maya (eng-platform): short list — 1) <10% request error rate on production routes (5xx) during and after the event, 2) cold-start tail latency <2x baseline for 90% of requests within 5m of failover, 3) fallback to on-demand pool within configured SLO (<= 90s), 4) no data-plane auth failures, 5) telemetry/alerts must surface root cause (eviction vs net partition).

Priya (eng-infra): who triggers evictions and how are we simulating network partition?

Tomas (sre): evict-bot will simulate preempts by draining spot nodes and we will use the fabric test-rig to blackhole control-plane egress for 10 minutes. Sequence: 1) drain 20% spot nodes, 2) wait 3m, 3) drain another 40%, 4) apply network egress deny to kube-apiserver for the control-plane VPC for 10m, 5) heal.

Priya (eng-infra): noted. evict commands (will run from staging account):

```
# cordon + drain example
kubectl --context=cluster-west2 get nodes -l pool=spot -o name | sh -c 'for n in $(cat); do kubectl --context=cluster-west2 cordon $n && kubectl --context=cluster-west2 drain $n --skip-daemonsets --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force; done'
```

Maya (eng-platform): autoscaler annotation we expect in this test (so scaling decisions are visible in traces):

```
annotations:
  horizontal-pod-autoscaler.k8s.io/estimated-target: "true"
  redwood.io/eviction-policy: "prefer-on-demand-after-90s"
```

evict-bot: starting spot eviction sequence (simulated) — draining 6 nodes (20% of pool) at 14:01:12

deploy-bot: rolling push for canary route paused (safety) :warning:

Jordan (eng-sre): watching logs and k8s events. adding an on-call bookmark. Will surface any 5xx spikes.

Tomas (sre): control-plane egress deny applied at 14:05:30 — simulating partition to AWS metadata and our control plane for 10m. This will cause kubelet->apiserver writes to fail (will not terminate pods but scaling controllers may be impacted).

Priya (eng-infra): seeing autoscaler activity — provisioning on-demand instances in us-west2. Cloud console shows new on-demand nodes in progress (ETA ~75s).

Maya (eng-platform): excellent — check that model-serving pods pick up KV cache warmup after reschedule. watch for ModelServing logs: 'kvcache: restored 82% prefixes'

Jordan (eng-sre): observed a transient errors spike ~14:06:20 (2m window) to 7% 5xx on /v1/generate but dropped back to 3% after on-demand nodes became Ready. Latency p95 increased 1.9x for ~4m.

Maya (eng-platform): within expected bounds. Note for postmortem — evaluate whether cache prepopulate can be sped up to reduce tail latency.

evict-bot: continuing sequence — draining another 12 nodes at 14:09:45 (total 60% of spot pool).

Tomas (sre): control-plane heal applied at 14:15:40. Observability note: apiserver error logs show short bursts of 'connection refused' from kubelets.

Priya (eng-infra): autoscaler stalled for ~40s when apiserver was unreachable, resumed after heal. Suggest adding a leader-election fallback to allow nodes to register via a cached API proxy.

Jordan (eng-sre): can we tag the episodes in tracing? I pushed a span attribute evict.test=true for the whole run. Helps slice traces.

Maya (eng-platform): yes, saved. Also created a metric dashboard to compare cost delta: pre-test baseline vs test-window. Initial numbers: estimated extra on-demand spend ~+12% for the 30m window.

Priya (eng-infra): deployment note — replica sets with poddisruptionbudgets prevented full restore of pods on some stateful workloads; had to relax PDBs for the duration. Marking as follow-up.

Tomas (sre): quick checklist items from run: 
- Add autoscaler fallback when apiserver unavailable
- Improve KV cache warmup by checkpointing to PVC + prefetch hooks
- Reduce autoscaler cooldown to allow faster on-demand burst (but watch cost)
- Add synthetic traffic to warm canary endpoints during failover

Maya (eng-platform): agreed. Assigning owners: autoscaler fallback -> Jordan, KV cache warmup -> Priya, PDB guidance -> Maya. I'll file a short postmortem with timelines.

Jordan (eng-sre): good drill. Learned that network partitions amplify autoscaler lag more than raw spot evictions.

Priya (eng-infra): one more datapoint — no auth tokens were dropped which is good, but internal control-plane metrics were delayed ~120s and confused some alert rules. We'll tune alert STT.

Maya (eng-platform): thanks all :thumbsup: — postmortem draft expected by EOD. If you observed logs/snippets to include, paste them here.

Tomas (sre): adding two quick snippets to include in postmortem:
```
14:06:17 request-id=abc123 route=/v1/generate status=502 downstream=eviction-sim source=node-42
14:07:22 kvcache: checkpoint failed: apiserver timeout (t=3s) recovering from pod move
```

Maya (eng-platform): copied. evict-bot: final state — simulation complete at 14:30:00, all spot nodes cleaned and on-demand fallback active.

deploy-bot: canary resume allowed.

Jordan (eng-sre): final checks — errors returned to baseline, new nodes stable, cost spike accounted. marking this game day as SUCCESS with follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

Maya (eng-platform): closing thread — thanks everyone. Postmortem link will go into #postmortems and a short blameless summary in the weekly infra notes.
